products.name: PCD (Portable Context Deck)
products.note: Portable context layer served over MCP; preferences, traits, skills, work state and knowledge in one deck loaded into any MCP-capable client; AGPL-3.0 public core; early access

profile_text.body:
Portable Context AI is a Belgium-based service operated by Andrea Dellanoce, offering a product called PCD, or Portable Context Deck. The company describes PCD as a portable context layer that a user sets up once and loads into any AI client that supports custom MCP connections, so that preferences, traits, skills, active work state, and a queryable knowledge base travel with the user across sessions and across different AI tools. The site presents PCD as being in early access at version 0.4, with self-serve signup available in controlled batches, and describes the service as currently free and capped, with a commitment not to introduce charges without first disclosing price and terms.

A deck is structured as a container with distinct components: preferences covering how a user likes to work, traits as standing guidelines handed to the AI at the start of each session, skills as saved procedures the AI can run on command, live work state so no session starts cold, a versioned history allowing rollback of committed decks and skills, specialised sub-contexts called specialists, and an experimental connections layer for mapping databases, tools, and APIs onto the deck. The MCP endpoint is published at https://mcp.portablecontext.ai/mcp and uses streamable HTTP transport with OAuth 2.0 and PKCE, requiring no API key. The public core of the software is published under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0, though the site notes the snapshot is not packaged as a runnable self-hosted distribution and that the managed service and private product capabilities fall outside the repository. External code contributions are not currently accepted pending a contributor licence agreement.

The terms of service and privacy policy, both effective 2026-08-13, confirm Belgian law applies and that complaints may be directed to the Belgian Data Protection Authority. Named data processors include Cloudflare, Supabase, Resend, and Sampark Inc trading as Composio. Server logs are retained for seven days, decks can be exported to JSON or Markdown at any time, and the policy states that private context is not sold and is not used to train or fine-tune any model. The minimum age to use the service is 16.
